name: HAMILTON SUNDSTRAND CORPORATION
naics_description: OTHER AIRCRAFT PARTS AND AUXILIARY EQUIPMENT MANUFACTURING
brief_text:
Four detectors flagged Hamilton Sundstrand Corporation. Benford's Law analysis found the distribution of leading digits in award amounts significantly deviates from expected patterns, with too few awards starting in 1 and too many in 2 and 3. Modification growth on contract SPRPA119GCE01 expanded at a rate nearly 46 times faster than peers in the same industry. The Isolation Forest algorithm identified the entity as a multivariate outlier based on its concentrated agency relationships and high modification frequency. Sole-source concentration showed the entity receives substantially more sole-source awards than typical competitors.

The Benford test yielded a KS statistic of 0.102 with p-value 4.1e-18 across 1,943 transactions. The worst modification contract grew at a ratio of 2,291 compared to a NAICS average of 50, producing a z-score of 8.02. The Isolation Forest anomaly score was 0.918 on a 0-1 scale. For sole-source work, the entity won 1,764 of 1,943 awards (90.8 percent sole-source) versus a peer median of 45.5 percent, yielding a z-score of 1.17.

These statistical signals warrant scrutiny but do not confirm fraud. Benford deviations can arise from legitimate business practices like tiered pricing or contract structures. As a major aerospace supplier with $789 million in lifetime obligations, Hamilton Sundstrand operates in a concentrated market where sole-source awards to established primes are common. The modification growth spike may reflect normal contract evolution rather than scope creep. The peer group for sole-source comparison includes 322 entities of varying size and specialization, which may mask legitimate differences in business model.
